answer.evidence: The refs handoff_refs/A.txt and B.txt only say to prioritize the file that best answers the request. They give no file-specific priority. I took A and B as the files they name, so the shared preference applies to C and D, which get 50 of the 60 minutes. radon/metrics.py holds the conversion in halstead_visitor_report (lines 69-94). Volume is N*log2(h) and is guarded with `if h != 0 else 0`. Difficulty is (h1*N2)/(2*h2) and is guarded with `if h2 != 0 else 0`. Effort is difficulty*volume, time is effort/18, and bugs is volume/3000. The zero-count cases and the log of a vocabulary of 1 (volume 0) need the closest check. mi_compute (lines 98-112) also guards volume <= 0 before taking a log. radon/visitors.py builds the operator and operand counts and the vocabulary and length totals that feed these formulas, so it gets the second-largest share. radon/raw.py and radon/complexity.py do not compute Halstead values, so they get only a short check. I did not read visitors.py, so I have not confirmed how it builds the counts.
